title: Effect of weak positional disorder on the miniband structure of spherical quantum dot chains
abstract: A theoretical framework is developed for the electron miniband structure in one-dimensional chains of spherical quantum dots subjected to weak positional disorder. Within the tight-binding approximation combined with the effective-medium approach, the stochastic fluctuations of the inter-dot spacing are mapped onto the renormalization of the key Hamiltonian parameters: the hopping integral $ B $, the overlap integral $ Q $, and the on-site energy shift $ M $. Analytical expressions for these disorder-renormalized parameters are derived by performing an ensemble average over a narrow Gaussian distribution of positional deviations ($ σ\ll a $). The resulting generalized dispersion relation shows that weak positional disorder causes a broadening of the minibands. Specifically, for typical fabrication fluctuations $σ= 0.1\,a $, the miniband width increases by 8-12\% (depending on the mean inter-dot distance $a$). At the same time, the sensitivity of the miniband width to disorder decreases rapidly with increasing lattice period due to the exponential decay of the electron wave functions. In the considered weak-disorder regime, the Anderson localization length significantly exceeds the lattice constant, so the miniband states remain delocalized.
summary: This theoretical paper analyzes the effect of weak positional disorder on the miniband structure of 1D chains of quantum dots using a tight-binding model. By averaging over Gaussian fluctuations, the authors show that disorder broadens the energy bands but does not induce localization in the weak regime. This work is vital for understanding the robustness of electronic transport in imperfect nanoscale materials.
main_problem: The study aims to elucidate how weak positional disorder affects the electronic miniband structure within one-dimensional chains of spherical quantum dots.
main_result: Weak positional disorder causes a measurable broadening of the minibands, although the states remain delocalized because the Anderson localization length significantly exceeds the lattice constant in this regime.
method: The authors developed a theoretical framework using the tight-binding approximation combined with an effective-medium approach to average over Gaussian fluctuations in inter-dot spacing.
model_or_system: The system modeled is a one-dimensional chain of spherical quantum dots (e.g., GaAs QDs) embedded in a matrix, treated as an infinite periodic structure subjected to small random positional deviations ($\sigma$).
key_observables: Miniband width ($W$), disorder-renormalized Hamiltonian parameters ($\langle M angle, \langle B angle, \langle Q angle$), and the Anderson localization length ($\xi_{loc}$).
important_parameters: Weak disorder regime ($\sigma \ll a$); low temperatures ($T 	o 0$ K); Gaussian distribution for positional deviations.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the nearest-neighbor approximation, assuming weak disorder ($\sigma \ll a$), and neglecting finite temperature effects.
figures_summary: Figure 2 compares ideal vs. disordered minibands; Figure 3 shows how the miniband width changes with lattice period ($a$) for both cases.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theoretical framework, derives averaged effective dispersion relations by incorporating disorder corrections ($\sigma^2$), and then analyzes the resulting broadening effects on key observables like the miniband width.
why_interesting: This work provides quantitative predictions for how structural imperfections (disorder) modify fundamental electronic band properties in nanoscale quantum structures, which is crucial for designing reliable solid-state quantum devices.
